If your last safe-output call already performed the final requested action and no further work or tool calls remain, it satisfies this requirement. Otherwise, call `noop` with a brief completion/no-additional-action message when the work is complete, or `report_incomplete` when it is not. Earlier safe-output calls do not satisfy this final-step requirement. Do NOT end your response without this terminal signal.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9213908Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9217832Z Safe-output calls are write-once declarations for real downstream side effects. Do NOT use them for probing, auth tests, retries with placeholder content, or "let me see if this works" experiments. If the task is complete but no real output is needed, call `noop`; if you cannot safely emit the intended real output, call `report_incomplete` with the blocker instead of trying variants.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9220365Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9223163Z **Tool retry limit:** if a safe-output tool (for example `push_to_pull_request_branch` or `close_pull_request`) fails, try at most 2 materially different recovery approaches. If the tool still fails, call `report_incomplete` with the error and the approaches attempted, then continue with other work. Do NOT debug underlying infrastructure after repeated failures.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9226512Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9230289Z **Trust successful tool responses.** Safeoutputs records write transactions that are applied after the agent finishes. A successful safe-output tool call means the transaction was accepted for downstream application. Do NOT independently verify the effect via `gh`, `gh api`, or other GitHub read paths from the current sandbox, because those paths will not reflect future safe-output writes.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9233543Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9236517Z **Do not inspect infrastructure internals.** When a tool or command fails, do not inspect Docker sockets (`/var/run/docker.sock`), mount tables (`/proc/self/mounts`), container networking (`/proc/net`), `/host` paths, git object storage internals, or container-runtime environment internals. These are outside your control; use `report_incomplete` after the retry limit.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9240568Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9246297Z temporary_id: optional cross-reference field only for tools whose input schema declares it, including create_issue, create_discussion, and create_pull_request. Do not add it to other tools. Canonical form: '#aw_' followed by 3–12 alphanumeric or underscore characters — e.g., '#aw_abc1', '#aw_pr_fix'. Pattern: /^#?aw_[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,12}$/i (the '#' prefix is optional; bare 'aw_abc1' is accepted and normalised to '#aw_abc1' automatically). Use this form in target fields only where their schema explicitly supports temporary IDs (item_number, issue_number, parent, etc.). In body/markdown text, '#aw_abc1' references are replaced with the real issue/PR/discussion number after creation. Omit entirely when not needed.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9250463Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9259507Z **Payloads**: safeoutputs tools do NOT support `@filename` expansion. For CLI calls, prefer a complete JSON object inline as one single-quoted shell argument. Inside JSON strings, encode newlines as `\n`, double quotes as `\"`, backslashes as `\\`, and apostrophes as `\u0027`; Unicode can remain literal. Stdin is also supported: `safeoutputs <tool_name> .` reads a complete JSON object from stdin — the entire stdin content must itself be valid JSON; never pipe a raw file or raw Markdown into this bare form. To pass one field's raw text verbatim with no JSON escaping, target that single field instead: `cat file.md | safeoutputs <tool_name> --<field> .` substitutes the field's value with the raw stdin text. Never write a bare `.` as a value inside a quoted JSON literal (e.g. `{"body": .}`) — that is not valid JSON. Do not use auxiliary shell commands or temporary files to construct payloads; the `cat file | ... --field .` form above is the one sanctioned exception, for raw-text fields only. When a native safe-output function is explicitly exposed, pass the fields directly.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9266379Z </safe-outputs>
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9266848Z <safe-output-tools>

2026-11-21T08:10:42.9268201Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9268419Z **Creating a Pull Request**
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9268748Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9268958Z To create a pull request:
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9269562Z 1. Make any file changes directly in the working directory.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9270774Z 2. If you haven't done so already, create a new local branch using `git checkout -b <branch-name>` with an appropriate unique name.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9274391Z 3. Add and commit your changes to the branch. Be careful to add exactly the files you intend, and check there are no extra files left un-added. Verify you haven't deleted or changed any files you didn't intend to.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9276397Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9277959Z 5. Create the pull request with the create_pull_request tool from safeoutputs exactly once, only when the final title/body/branch are ready.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9279741Z 6. After calling `create_pull_request`, STOP. Do not probe with another PR call, do not test auth with manual `git push`, and do not rewrite git remotes.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9280740Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9283417Z **Important**: The `branch` parameter in the create_pull_request tool **must exactly match the name of your current local git branch** — the branch you just committed to. You can verify this with `git branch --show-current`. Never invent or guess a branch name; always use the actual branch name from `git branch --show-current`. If you are on an existing branch (e.g. you checked out a PR branch), use that branch name.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9288114Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9289943Z **Important**: `create_pull_request` is not a sandbox. Every successful call records a real PR intent that can become an externally visible pull request. Never use placeholder payloads like `"test"` / `"test"` to see what happens. If you are not ready to open the real PR, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9292650Z </safe-output-tools>

2026-11-21T08:10:42.9308492Z

2026-11-21T08:10:42.9321325Z

Inside JSON strings, encode newlines as `\n`, double quotes as `\"`, backslashes as `\\`, and apostrophes as `\u0027` so they do not end the shell quote. Unicode can remain literal. The binary comes first, so a malformed payload still runs the CLI and reports an error:
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9327583Z ```bash

2026-11-21T08:10:42.9331249Z ```
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9333849Z This preserves multiline content without auxiliary tools, pipelines, temporary files, or shell expansion. Adapt fields to the enabled tool's schema. Raw Markdown and `@filename` references are not JSON payloads.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9335583Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9341678Z Stdin is also supported: `safeoutputs <tool_name> .` reads a complete JSON object from stdin — the entire stdin content must itself be valid JSON; never pipe a raw file or raw Markdown into this bare form. Never write a bare `.` as a value inside a quoted JSON literal (e.g. `{"body": .}`) — that is not valid JSON. CLI proxying grants the mounted executable, not auxiliary commands, file writes, or shell expansions beyond the `cat file | ... --field .` form above. Stdin support does not grant permission for redirections. Prefer inline JSON; do not use auxiliary shell commands to construct or submit it.

2026-11-21T08:10:42.9510275Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9510604Z 1. Run the retrieval and the comparison, in this order:
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9511091Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9511285Z    ```sh
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9511916Z    python3 .agents/skills/sync-festival/scripts/sync_festival.py fetch

2026-11-21T08:10:42.9551487Z    python3 .agents/skills/sync-festival/scripts/sync_festival.py apply
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9552246Z    ```
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9552482Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9552910Z    The Apify token is already in the environment as `APIFY_TOKEN`. Never write it
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9553777Z    to a file, a commit or the pull request.

2026-11-21T08:10:42.9554833Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9555028Z    ```sh
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9556201Z    python3 .agents/skills/sync-festival/scripts/sync_festival.py check

2026-11-21T08:10:42.9558686Z    ```
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9558922Z 
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9559362Z 3. Resolve what the report still lists under "Needs your review", but only where
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9647200Z    the sources let you. The rules are in the skill's ground rules: a curated
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9667293Z    per-day schedule stays; a conflict between the site and a post stays; a slug
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9678880Z    that needs a map pin stays. Do not invent a value.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9679446Z

2026-11-21T08:10:42.9680790Z    stop. Do not open an empty pull request.

2026-11-21T08:10:42.9682251Z

2026-11-21T08:10:42.9683426Z    - Body: the **full, unmodified contents of `tmp/sync/report.md`**, pasted as
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9684377Z      Markdown, followed by one line naming the commands that ran.
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9694640Z    - Commit only `src/events.json`, `src/index.md`, `src/llms.txt` and the two
2026-11-21T08:10:42.9696257Z      HTML wrappers when they changed. `tmp/` is gitignored and must stay out.
